typical_mindset: Acute and obtuse are remembered as a pair of opposite labels without a firm anchor to which one means 'smaller than a right angle' and which means 'bigger' — the labels get swapped even when the underlying comparison-to-90-degrees idea is understood.
explanation_strategy: Anchor both labels to the right angle (90 degrees) as the dividing line, using a concrete comparison, rather than asking the child to recall the definitions directly.

example_dialogue.text: Is this angle bigger or smaller than a right angle (like the corner of a book)?
Right — angles smaller than a right angle are called acute. So what would you call this one?

source: Topic-authored; no direct literature-survey citation for acute/obtuse label confusion specifically.
